evidence.requirements: Almost every requirement is met. The start page has the 'Cartridges' heading, name links, family, L3, 'Search' and 'Family' controls with the exact options, and '<n> cartridges' (list.jpg; app.js:25-66). Search finds alternative names; '7,62 x 51' returns 308 Win. (model.js:77-86). The detail view has all the facts, a source link for water capacity, Symbol/Value/Unit tables grouped by section, tolerances next to their values ('39.62 -0.2' in detail-308_win.jpg), Print and 'All cartridges', and a hash address that survives a reload (model.js:100-124). The drawing is an inline SVG at 1 unit = 1 mm with aria-label '<name> drawing', a hatched section, a dash-dot centre line, a title block, and the required dimensions labelled 'L3 51.18' and 'α 40°'. Rule 9 notes are shown (geometry.js:226-230). Print is one A4 page with a source footer (print-308_win.jpg). Partly met: the diameter dimensions have no extension lines; the dimension line runs through the part with the arrows on the outline (drawing.js:235-244). Phone legibility is only logged in verify.js:110, not asserted, and the drawing text works out to roughly 8 px at 360 px width. The Unit column repeats '°' after values that already end in '°' ('40° °').
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Chamfer: geometry.js:154-160. Rimfire half-round with radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2): 161-171. Groove floor and straight ramp to (P1/2,E): 192-206. Belt ramp at δ to R3/2, then to E, then a step in: 200-204. Straight versus bottleneck body and fillets with r1 min and r2: 216-232. Bullet seating, k, meplat, tangent ogive, quarter ellipse and cones match rule 7 (geometry.js:78-98). The heeled bullet uses H2 outside and H2-2·tb inside (89-90). Walls, w and primer pocket match rule 8 (239-276). The screenshots agree with the reference outlines in proportion: the 308 bottleneck, the 300 WM belt flush with the rim (R3=R1), the 9 mm taper and round nose, the 22 LR rounded rim and heel, the 9,3x74R shallow 10°58' shoulder, and the 44 Mag semi-wadcutter cone. Label values match the data. Small deviations: for heeled cases tn is set to tb, and straight cases blend tb to tn over an invented 2 mm (STRAIGHT_TRANSITION, geometry.js:13), both undocumented interpretations. The α marker is a ray drawn outward from A plus an arc, not across the flank (drawing.js:247-259). The 'Scale 1.79 : 1 (A4 print)' text is true only in print.
evidence.security: The SVG goes in through figure.innerHTML (app.js:82), but every data string in it is passed through esc() (drawing.js:26, 55, 61, 289-290), and numbers go through fmt(). All other DOM content is built with createElement and textContent (app.js:8-22). There is no eval, Function or timer strings. There are no external requests; e2e asserts this (app.test.js:57), and verify.js:126 checks it again.
evidence.code_quality: The modules are clear: format, model, geometry and drawing are pure and testable in a vm context (tests/helpers/load.js), and app.js handles the DOM. Naming follows the brief's symbols. Missing values produce notes instead of crashes. The drawing's render() is one ~270-line function full of magic constants (FS, PITCH, offsets) and dense one-liners, which is hard to read. The heel and straight-case wall decisions live in code with no comments explaining why.
evidence.tests: The unit tests check each geometry rule against computed values. Rim type, chamfer and groove points (geometry.test.js:15-51); fillet tangency; belt ramp end (87-98); rimfire half-round (100-112); ogive circle, ellipse and cone collinearity (121-163); walls, w and pocket per primer (165-184); heeled bullet (194-205); rule 9 (207-227); invariants for all 25 records (234-254). The drawing tests check for label overlaps against all lines for every record, with Liang-Barsky clipping (drawing.test.js:83-99), the viewBox, scale and α included angle. The e2e tests cover the file:// and http flows, search, filter, reload, back and no external requests. verify.js checks one-page A4 PDFs, real-font collisions, print colours and phone overflow for all 25.
evidence.ux_design: Information is dense and calm. The fact grid is compact, the tables are tight with tabular numbers and right-aligned values, and tolerances are greyed next to their values. The drawing labels are large and clear with no overlaps in any screenshot. Print is well thought out: 5-column facts, a full-width drawing and 4-column tables on one page (print-308_win.jpg). Weaknesses: the title block is oversized next to the part. Short cartridges (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg) fill only about 35% of the figure, leaving a large empty box. The head diameters R1, E1 and P1 sit in a tight cluster of vertical lines and arrows.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, an aria-label and a <title>, plus a <desc> giving rim type, L3 and L6 (drawing.js:287-290). That text alternative is thin, but the full values are in the tables. The tables have captions and th scope=col (app.js:64, 70-72). The inputs have <label for>, the count is aria-live (app.js:30), the toolbar is an aria-labelled nav, h1 receives focus on route change, and :focus-visible outlines are styled. Muted text #5a6572 on #fbfbfa passes AA. Dark mode uses prefers-color-scheme (style.css:18-30).
evidence.simplicity: There are no runtime dependencies. Plain scripts total about 800 lines of app JS for a non-trivial geometry and dimensioning problem. The only dev dependency is Playwright. There is no needless abstraction.
evidence.maintainability: The README gives the file map and the commands (npm test, test:e2e, verify), and a lockfile exists. However, there is no CI pipeline, no engines field or .nvmrc pinning Node 22, and Playwright is a caret range. There are no ADRs in the repo, and the README points to docs/superpowers/specs and plans that are not in the repository. There is no versioning or release notes beyond 1.0.0. The interpretation choices (heel wall, straight-case wall blend, label placement constants) are not documented outside the code.
evidence.visual_design: Typography is restrained: system sans, uppercase small labels, monospace symbols and tabular numbers. Colours are calm, with a single accent. The detail pages look consistent with each other (all detail screenshots). The drawing line weights are sensible (0.35 outline, 0.18 dims). The title block font is large for the drawing size, and the big empty figure area on short cartridges makes those pages look unfinished.
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is clear: name, facts, drawing, then the cartridge and chamber tables. There is no clipping or overlap in any screenshot. The print layout fits one A4 page with room to spare (print-308_win.jpg). Space is used poorly in the figure for short cases because of the 106 mm minimum width (drawing.js:17), and the auto-fill table grid leaves ragged gaps (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg).
evidence.usability: Search as you type, the family filter kept in the URL, back-navigation that keeps filter state (app.test.js:36-42), bookmarkable detail URLs, a not-found page with a way back, and one-click print. Few steps for every task. The drawing on a phone would need zooming to read its labels.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would find it credible. Values appear as published with tolerances, the drawings are computed and true to scale with C.I.P.-style symbols, the source is stated, and the printout is clean and dense. The empty-looking figures for pistol and rimfire cartridges and the oversized title block slightly reduce the polish.

unmet_requirements: Diameter dimensions (R1, E1, P1, P2, H1, H2, G1) have no extension lines; the dimension line runs through the part (drawing.js:235-244)
Phone legibility of the drawing is not verified, only logged (verify.js:110); at 360 px the label text is about 8 px
Unit column repeats '°' for angles whose value already carries '°'
strengths: The geometry follows the brief's rules 1-9 faithfully for every family shown (chamfer, groove, belt, rimfire half-round, fillets, ogive/ellipse/cone noses, heeled bullet, walls, pocket), and the outlines match the reference drawings in proportion
Very strong tests: per-rule numeric unit tests, label/line collision checks across all 25 records, e2e over file:// and http, and a verify script checking one-page A4 print and print colours
Clean, dependency-free, offline app with escaped SVG output, bookmarkable routes, and a precise one-page print layout
issues: Poor use of space in the drawing figure: the 106 mm minimum width and large title block leave short cartridges (9 mm Luger, 22 LR, 44 Rem. Mag.) filling only about a third of the figure, and on a phone the labels would be about 8 px

Maintainability gaps: no CI, no Node version pin, the README points to spec and plan docs that are missing from the repo, and interpretation choices (heel wall, 2 mm straight-case wall blend) are undocumented
Diameter dimensions lack extension lines and cluster tightly at the head (R1/E1/P1); the α marker is drawn unconventionally, and the angle Unit column repeats the degree sign
review.verdict: This is a well-engineered, faithful implementation: the computed drawings follow the brief's geometry rules, match the references, and print legibly on one A4 page, all backed by unusually thorough tests. It is close to publishable; the main things to fix are the wasted figure space and phone legibility for short cartridges, plus missing CI and documentation.
